experiment: Full-sweep per-cell decomposition analysis: does overall-accuracy improvement in corrected-trained models (vs standard-trained) reflect genuine balanced discrimination, and is any such effect uniform across early/mid/late swap positions or concentrated in some? Specifically: does any cell escape the two distinct SMF2 bagcount-ffn failure modes (h8-style accept-bias, h32-style reject-bias) into genuine balanced_any territory?
important_bagcount_failure_mode_note: SMF2 found two DISTINCT failure modes for the shortcut-only bagcount-ffn baseline, not a smooth capacity trend: h8 (plus shortcut/ngram) collapses to ACCEPT-bias (hard_negative_accuracy=0.00), h32/h128/h512 flip to near-total REJECT-bias (hard_negative_accuracy~0.99, positive_accuracy near 0, overall pinned at ~0.50). Neither is genuine discrimination. balanced_any (BOTH positive_accuracy > 0.5 AND hard_negative_accuracy > 0.5) is the only criterion that counts -- a corrected-trained cell matching or exceeding h32's 0.99 hard-negative accuracy while its positive_accuracy stays near 0 is just landing in the same reject-bias failure mode, not genuine progress.
